 J U D G M E N T

The Assistant Commissioner of Police, Kengeri Gate Sub-Division, Bangalore City, has submitted charge sheet against the accused persons for the offence punishable U/s.498A and 304-B r/w.34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act in Crime No.145/2017 of Byatarayanapura P.S.
2.

sentences.text:
The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The marriage between the accused No.1 and deceased Smt.Asha was performed on 21.05.2015 at Yediyur according to the customs prevailed in their community.
At the time of marriage, both accused Nos.1 and 2 being the brothers demanded and received gold ring, chain, bracelet and 110 gms of gold to the deceased as dowry.
After marriage, as the accused No.1 serving in the Indian Army at Gujarat, hence started their marital life at his working place.
At that juncture, the accused has harassed the deceased physically and mentally by demanding additional dowry from her mother.
Due to the marital relationship, the deceased has become pregnant and returned to her parental house for delivery and gave birth to a male child.
On 18.04.2017, the accused returned from Gujarat and went to the parental house of deceased to return to his work place alongwith his wife and son.
On 20.04.2017 came to the house of his brother i.e. accused No.2 alongwith his wife and son i.e. male child situated at No.10/2, 2 nd cross,, Raghavanagar, Timber Yard Layout, Mysore road.

On that day at about 8.30 p.m both accused Nos.1 and 2 picked up quarrel with the deceased and harassed her physically and mentally by demanding additional dowry, due to which the deceased become anguish, went inside the room and locked and committed suicide by hanging with the help of veil to the iron rod of the ventilator and succumbed to death.
Thereby the accused persons have committed the offences as alleged against them.
3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned ACMM., Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing copy of charge sheet to the accused.

The same was numbered as SC No.1213/2017.
4.
The prosecution has examined sixteen witnesses as PW.1 to PW.16 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to P23 and MO.1 to 6.
The learned PP has gave up the witnesses C.W.18 to 22, 24 to 26 in view of evidence of other witnesses.

The court has issued warrant, summons and proclamation to CWs.9,
12 to 15, but the concerned police completely failed to execute the warrant and keep present the said witness before the court to record their evidence.
As such the prayer of the learned public prosecutor was rejected and the witnesses C.Ws.9, 12 to 15 were dropped.
5. After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statements of accused persons, as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.

2 present against them and not claimed any defense evidence nor submitted anything to Court.

sentences.text: The accused persons have complied application u/s.437A of Cr.PC by executing personal bond and surety bond.

6. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
7.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:
1. Whether the prosecution proves that 21.05.2015 the accused married the deceased Smt.Asha, sister of informant at Yediyur, as per the customs prevailed in their community, and at the time of marriage accused No.1 being husband and accused No.2 being the brother-in-law of deceased- Smt. Asha on demand received gold ring, gold chain, gold bracelet and 110 grams of gold to the deceased as dowry and thereby accused No.1 and 2 have committed an offence punishable U/s.3 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 ?
2. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 and 2 are being the husband and brother-in-law of deceased-Smt. Asha, and after the marriage, when the deceased started to reside along with accused No.1 at Gujarath State, and on 18.04.2017 accused No.1 came to the parental house of deceased to take deceased -Smt. Asha to back Gujarat along with child and on 20.04.2017 while on his way to Gujarat, accused No.1 took deceased and child to the house of accused No.2 bearing No.10/2, situated at 2nd Cross, Raghavanagara, Timber yard Mysore Road, within the limits of Byatarayanapura P.S., Bangalore, and at about 8.30 p.m. on 20.04.2017 accused No.1 and 2 picked up quarrel with the deceased-Smt. Asha by subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty by demanding additional dowry from her mother and thereby accused No.1 and 2 have committed an offence punishable U/s.4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 ?
3. Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 and 2 are being the husband and brother-in-law of deceased -Smt.Asha with common intention to commit an offence, and on 18.04.2017 accused No.1 came to the parental house of deceased to take deceased -Smt. Asha to back Gujarat along with child and on 20.04.2017 while on his way to Gujarat, accused No.1 took deceased and child to house of accused No.2 bearing No.10/2, situated at 2nd Cross, Raghavanagara, Timber yard, Mysore Road, within the limits of Byatarayanapura P.S., Bangalore, and at about 8.30 p.m. on 20.04.2017 accused No.1 and 2 picked up up quarrel with the deceased-Smt. Asha by subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty by demanding additional dowry from her mother and thereby accused No.1 and 2 have committed an offence punishable U/s.498A r/w Sec.34 of of Indian Penal Code, 1860?
4.

Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 and 2 are being the husband and brother-in-law of deceased-Smt.Asha with common intention to commit an offence, and on 18.04.2017 accused No.1 came to the parental house of deceased to take deceased -Smt. This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: In the Negative  Point No.4: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S 9. Points No.1 to 3: These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.

On perusal of the prosecution papers, the documents marked at Ex.P.3 and 4 i.e. marriage invitation and photos clearly demonstrate that the accused No.1 and deceased were legally wedded husband and wife.
It is also an admitted fact that their marriage was performed on 21.05.2015.

The main allegation of the prosecution against these accused persons is that before marriage, both accused persons received dowry to the deceased on demand and even after marriage when the deceased started her marital life with accused No.1 at his working place at Gujarat, where the accused No.1 subjected her to physical and mental cruelty.

On the date of alleged incident also, both accused persons harassed the deceased physically and mentally at the residence of accused No.2 and due to which the deceased was fed up and committed suicide.

To prove the said allegations the prosecution succeeded to examine Ajay Kumar, brother of the deceased as P.W.1, Shantamma mother of the deceased as P.W.7, Shruthi younger sister of the deceased as P.W.8.
On perusal of the evidence of PW.1, P.W.7 and P.W.8 nothing has been elicited by the prosecution regarding harassment as alleged against the accused persons.
According to these witnesses PW.1, P.W.7 and P.W.8, after marriage, both the accused No.1 and deceased living together happily.
These witnesses does not know the actual reasons why the deceased has committed suicide.
According to the complainant he has also not acquainted with the recitals of the complaint and the police have not seized any material objects at the time of conducting Mahazar at spot as per Ex.P.2.

It is the say of the P.W.1 that some relative have prepared the complaint as per Ex.P.1 and obtained his signature and the Byatarayanapura P.S vs A1 Mohan Kumar M.D on 29 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119181970/
4 police have not conduced Mahazar as per Ex.P.2 in his presence.

sentences.text: Since the evidence of the family members of the deceased being the prime witness of the prosecution deposed evidence contrary to the contents of complaint, spot Mahazar and to their respective statements, hence the learned PP treated the said witnesses P.W.1, P.W.7 and P.W.8 as hostile with the permission of the court and cross-examined.
Unfortunately the learned PP was not able to bring out the actual reasons or cause for committing of suicide by the deceased.
So, there is no any piece of evidence placed by the prosecution through family members of the deceased to believe because of dowry harassment, the deceased has committed suicide.
As such the evidence of P.W1, PW.7 and P.W.8 not at all worthful for the prosecution to prove the allegations made against the accused persons.
10. In this case, the prosecution examined both panchas to the spot Mahazar marked at Ex.P.2.
The pancha Shivamade Gowda and Gundaiah examined as PW.2 and P.W.3 respectively, since they are the signatories to the spot Mahazar.

Both witnesses PW.2 and P.W.3 though admitted their signatures present on Ex.P.2, but it is the say of the said witness that the police have obtained their signatures on road and nothing has been seized from the spot in their presence.

Even though the said Mahazar Ex.P.2 reveals the seizure of veil by the Investigation Officer, since the evidence of P.W.2 and P.W.3 not in accordance with the recitals of the panchanama Ex.P.2, hence learned PP has cross-examined both PW.2 and P.W.3 treating them as hostile with the permission of the court,
but both the panchas failed to admit the suggestions of the learned PP.
In the cross-examination of accused counsel, both panchas admitted that they do not know the contents of Ex.P.2 and they signed the Ex.P.2 at the request of the police.

As such the evidence placed by the prosecution related to Mahazar Ex.P.2 through witnesses P.W.2 and P.W.3 not helpful for the prosecution to prove the Mahazar Ex.P.2.
11.

It is necessary to note that the panchas by name Nandisha and Vasanth Kumar examined as PW.9 and P.W.10 being the signatories to the seizure Mahazar marked at Ex.P.8 also not supported the prosecution story.
According to the witnesses PW.9 and P.W.10 the police have not seized the gold ornaments in their presence under Mahazar Ex.P.8 at Syndicate bank on 16.05.2017 in the presence of accused No.1.

As such the learned PP treated both the seizure panchas P.W.9 and P.W.10 as hostile and cross- examined, but not able to bring out any useful evidence to believe the concerned IO has carried out seizure Mahazar in their presence at Syndicate bank situated at Nagamangala.

Hence the evidence given by both the seizure panchas P.W.9 and P.W.10 not worthful for the prosecution to prove the said seizure Mahazar Ex.P.8.
12.

It is necessary to note that the Tahasildar by name Venkatachalapathy examined as P.W.14 has categorically deposed that on 21.04.2017 on the basis of the requisition received from the ACP,
Kengeri Gate Sub Division, conducted inquest Mahazar on the dead body of the deceased at the mortuary, KIMS Hospital.
The inquest Mahazar marked at Ex.P.5 and the requisition at Ex.P.11.
The said witness P.W.14 also recorded statement of the witness.

The said witness admitted not mentioning of the time on the requisition, also admitted the said requisition having the particulars of the case and on the basis of the said particulars prepared the Ex.P.5 inquest Mahazar in consonance with the contents of their requisition.
The said piece of evidence brought out during the cross-examination by the counsel for the accused certainly create doubt about his visit to the mortuary and conducting of inquest Mahazar.

sentences.text: 5 Mahazar by name Arun, Sridhar and Malluswamy examined at P.W.4 to P.W.6.
According to the evidence of said PW.4 to P.W.6, the Tahasildar has obtained their signatures to the inquest Mahazar, when they went to see the dead body of Asha.
The cross-examination of said witnesses PW.4 to P.W.6 denotes that they do not know what is written in the inquest Mahazar Ex.P.5.
Further admitted they have signed Ex.P.5 at the request of the police.
It clearly goes to show that these witnesses P.W.4 to PW.6 not at all aware anything about the contents of the inquest Mahazar marked at Ex.P.5.

So the prosecution has failed to place any reliable evidence to believe the conducting of inquest Mahazar by the witness P.W.14 in the presence of the witnesses PW.4 to P.W.6.
13.
It is necessary to note that P.W.11 is Dr.Jaganath.
The evidence of the said Dr.Jaganath reveals that he has carried out P.M on the dead body of deceased Asha and issued P.M.Report as per Ex.P.9.

The chief- examination of the said witness clearly explains about the presence of external injuries,
other relevant observations.
According to the opinion of the said doctor, the death was due to Asphyxia as a result of hanging.

Even though the evidence of the said doctor discloses that the blood has been sent for chemical analysis to FSL to know the presence of any poison/drugs, but the Investigation Officer Mr.Sajith, then ACP has failed to collect the FSL Report and produce before the court for the best reasons.

The cross-examination of the said witness P.W.11 shows that he is not aware anything about the conducting of inquest Mahazar by the Tahasildar before commencement of the post mortem on the dead body of the deceased.
The doctor has admitted not mentioning the age of the injuries in the P.M.Report Ex.P.9.
The rest of the evidence of the said doctor has completely denied by the counsel for the accused.

14. It is obvious to note that the witness P.W.12 T.P.Shivaswamy the then PSI deposed before the court on the basis of the complaint lodged by the complainant on 21.04.2017 at 5.30 a.m registered FIR as per Ex.P.10 vide Cr.No.145/2017 and handed over further investigation to the then ACP P.W.16 by name Sajith.
The said evidence has denied completely by the counsel for the accused.

Such being the case, during the course of investigation carried by P.W.16, the then ACP has issued Memo to the witnesses C.W.21, C.W.22 and C.W.23 to recover the gold articles pledged in the bank at Nagamangala by the accused.
On the basis of said Memo, they went to the said bank situated at Nagamangala alongwith accused and seized one gold ring and bracelet and accordingly carried out Mahazar as per Ex.P.8.
As already discussed supra, the signatories to the seizure Mahazar Ex.P.8 completely turned hostile.
On perusal of the documents produced by the Investigation Officer marked at Ex.P.19 shows that 3 items such as one hand chain, 2 ring, one pair hangings were pledged by the accused No.1.

There is no specific evidence placed by the prosecution through the Investigation Officer P.W.16, what happened to the remaining pledged gold articles because on careful scrutiny of Ex.P.19 discloses that on the said date when the properties were seized by the police account was also closed by the bank officials as per the endorsement.

There is no single documents collected by the Investigation Officer P.W.16 to erase the doubt related to the remaining pledged gold articles by the accused No.2, though it is the say of the Investigation Officer that they have seized only 2 articles as referred above for the investigation purpose.
Perhaps it is the duty of the Investigation Officer to verify and seize the properties required for the investigation and also note specifically what happened to the remaining pledged articles.
There is no such evidence placed by the prosecution to give clarity.

15. In this case, the Investigation Officer PW.16 who has taken the investigation of this case through PW.12 deposed before the court that on 21.04.2017 itself went to the spot at 9.00 a.m conducted Mahazar as per Ex.P.2 in the presence of panchas as shown by the complainant and seized red colour veil used by the deceased to hang herself.
The said Investigation Officer has not seized the lock because the prosecution papers shows that after locking the room, the deceased has committed suicide.
He has sent a requisition to the Spl. Tahasildar to carry out inquest Mahazar and he has recorded statement of the witnesses.
He has also sent requisition to the doctor to conduct Post Mortem.
He has also collected the marriage invitation, photos and also invoice for reserving the marriage hall from the complainant.
16. It is pertinent to note that on 22.04.2017, the accused No.2 was produced before him by C.W.22 and C.W.26 at 6.00 p.m.
The report submitted by C.W.26 has been marked at Ex.P.13.

He has also recorded statements of C.W.21 and C.W.22, who were deputed to trace the accused and also recorded the voluntary statement of accused on 23.04.2017, further he has produced accused No.1 before the court alongwith remand application.

The said Investigation Officer has not stated before the court whether the said accused was subjected to medical examination before producing before to the court alongwith the remand application as required under law.
The said Investigation Officer came to know that on 03.05.2017 the accused No.1 admitted in Command hospital.

As such he has sent requisition as per Ex.P.14 to get information about the health condition of accused No.1.
17.
It is necessary to note that on 11.05.2017 sent the requisition to C.W.18 to prepare sketch map.
On the same day, he has collected hospital records as per Ex.P.15.
In continuation of the further investigation on 12.05.2017, he has collected P.M.Report and articles present on dead body handed over during conducting of the Post Mortem as per Ex.P.9 from C.W.19.
The said articles were brought into P.F vide No.111/2017.
The clothes related to the deceased identified by this witness marked at M.O.2 to M.O.6.
On 15.05.2017, the PSI Hanumantharayappa, C.W.20 and C.W.25 produced the accused No.1 before him and the said PSI submitted report as per Ex.P.17.
He has carried out arrest procedure against said accused No.1 and recorded his voluntary statement.
On the basis of the voluntary statement of accused No.1, on 16.05.2017 issued Memo to C.W.27.

In view of Memo, the said witness C.W.27 alongwith accused No.1 and other police staff gone to Syndicate bank situated at Nagamangala and seized the pledged gold ornaments received by the said accused at the time of marriage.
The said Memo has been marked at Ex.P.18.
After producing the Mahazar carried by C.W.27 alongwith seized gold ornaments, the Investigation Officer has brought the same into the P.F.No113/2017.
The documents related to the pledging of gold articles has been identified by this witness marked at Ex.P.19.
On 16.05.2017, sent the seized articles shown in P.F.No.111/2017 to the FSL alongwith requisition as per Ex.P.20 received endorsement as per Ex.P.21.

On 17.05.2017 he recorded statement of CW.20, 23 and 27 and released gold ring and by receiving the indemnity bond as per Ex.P.22.
18.
It is obvious to note that on 15.06.2017 collected sketch as per Ex.P.23 related to the place of the incident by submitting requisition as per Ex.P.12.

sentences.text: In the cross-examination, the said witness has deposed that the complainant has signed Ex.P.2 i.e. spot Mahazar, but no signature of the complainant is present on the said document.

As per the version of the Investigation Officer P.W.16, as already discussed above, so far as seizure of gold bracelet and ring is concerned, there is discrepancy in the evidence of the Investigation Officer and other police witness and also prosecution papers.
The same is not properly explained by the Investigation Officer before the court.
The documents issued by the bank related to the pledging of articles marked at Ex.P.19 is not matches with the evidence of the Investigation Officer.
The contents of the seizure Mahazar Ex.P.8 and documents related to pledging of gold articles Ex.P.19 read together, it is very clear that both documents are contrary with each other.
The rest of the evidence of the Investigation Officer has completely denied by the counsel for the accused persons.

Apart from the evidence of Investigation Officer as already discussed above,
the evidence given by the independent witness completely against to the story of the prosecution and not corroborate with the evidence of the police official witness.
Hence, it is very clear that the prosecution has failed to place the material of evidence to prove the allegations made against the accused persons.
As such, this court has answered the point Nos.1 to 3 in the Negative.
19. Point No.4:

In view of answer of this court on points No.1 to 3, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused Nos.1 and 2 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 304-B r/w.34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The bail bonds and surety bonds of accused persons stand cancelled.
The M.O.1 to 6 clothes being worthless are ordered to be destroyed after the expiry of appeal time.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Assistant Commissioner of Police, Kengeri Gate Sub-Division, Bangalore City, has submitted charge sheet against the accused persons for the offence punishable U/s.498A and 304-B r/w.34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act in Crime No.145/2017 of Byatarayanapura P.S.
2.
At the time of marriage, both accused Nos.1 and 2 being the brothers demanded and received gold ring, chain, bracelet and 110 gms of gold to the deceased as dowry.
After marriage, as the accused No.1 serving in the Indian Army at Gujarat, hence started their marital life at his working place.
At that juncture, the accused has harassed the deceased physically and mentally by demanding additional dowry from her mother.
Due to the marital relationship, the deceased has become pregnant and returned to her parental house for delivery and gave birth to a male child.
On 18.04.2017, the accused returned from Gujarat and went to the parental house of deceased to return to his work place alongwith his wife and son.
On that day at about 8.30 p.m both accused Nos.1 and 2 picked up quarrel with the deceased and harassed her physically and mentally by demanding additional dowry, due to which the deceased become anguish, went inside the room and locked and committed suicide by hanging with the help of veil to the iron rod of the ventilator and succumbed to death.
Thereby the accused persons have committed the offences as alleged against them.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing copy of charge sheet to the accused.
The accused persons have complied application u/s.437A of Cr.PC by executing personal bond and surety bond.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the prosecution proves that the accused No.1 and 2 are being the husband and brother-in-law of deceased-Smt.Asha with common intention to commit an offence, and on 18.04.2017 accused No.1 came to the parental house of deceased to take deceased -Smt. Asha to back Gujarat along with child and on 20.04.2017 while on his way to Gujarat, accused No.1 took deceased and child to house of you accused No.2 bearing No.10/2, situated at 2nd Cross, Raghavanagara,

3 Timber yard Mysore Road, within the limits of Byatarayanapura P.S., Bangalore and at about 8.30 p.m. on 20.04.2017 accused No.1 and 2 picked up up quarrel with the deceased-Smt. Asha by subjecting her to physical and mental cruelty by demanding additional dowry from her mother and such cruelty and harassment as did drive the said deceased-Smt. Asha to commit suicide by hanging herself to the iron rod of Ventilator with the help of veil on 20.04.2017 during night hours at house bearing No.10/2, situated at 2nd Cross, Raghavanagara, Timber yard Mysore Road, within the limits of Byatarayanapura P.S., Bangalore, and accused No.1 and 2 being her husband and brother-in-law within a period of seven years of marriage, subjected her to cruelty and harassment for all in connection with the demand for dowry and thereby accused No.1 and 2 have committed an an offence of dowry death punishable U/s.304B r/w Sec.34 of Indian Penal Code,1860?
4. What order?
8.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The main allegation of the prosecution against these accused persons is that before marriage, both accused persons received dowry to the deceased on demand and even after marriage when the deceased started her marital life with accused No.1 at his working place at Gujarat, where the accused No.1 subjected her to physical and mental cruelty.
Since the evidence of the family members of the deceased being the prime witness of the prosecution deposed evidence contrary to the contents of complaint, spot Mahazar and to their respective statements, hence the learned PP treated the said witnesses P.W.1, P.W.7 and P.W.8 as hostile with the permission of the court and cross-examined.
Unfortunately the learned PP was not able to bring out the actual reasons or cause for committing of suicide by the deceased.
So, there is no any piece of evidence placed by the prosecution through family members of the deceased to believe because of dowry harassment, the deceased has committed suicide.
As such the evidence of P.W1, PW.7 and P.W.8 not at all worthful for the prosecution to prove the allegations made against the accused persons.
There is no single documents collected by the Investigation Officer P.W.16 to erase the doubt related to the remaining pledged gold articles by the accused No.2, though it is the say of the Investigation Officer that they have seized only 2 articles as referred above for the investigation purpose.
Perhaps it is the duty of the Investigation Officer to verify and seize the properties required for the investigation and also note specifically what happened to the remaining pledged articles.
There is no such evidence placed by the prosecution to give clarity.
The documents issued by the bank related to the pledging of articles marked at Ex.P.19 is not matches with the evidence of the Investigation Officer.
opennyai_summary.decision:
19. Point No.4:
In view of answer of this court on points No.1 to 3, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused Nos.1 and 2 are hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 304-B r/w.34 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.3 and 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
The bail bonds and surety bonds of accused persons stand cancelled.
The M.O.1 to 6 clothes being worthless are ordered to be destroyed after the expiry of appeal time.
